narrative: The model estimates a 71% chance that you will leave your job, and this is the reason you are being denied a promotion. The strongest signal driving this prediction is your total work experience: having 11 or more years overall makes you much more likely to leave compared to the typical employee predicted to stay, only about 15% of whom have that much experience. The second most important factor works in your favor: you reported no other job opportunities, which pushes the prediction toward staying, and most employees predicted to stay are in the same situation. However, this was not enough to offset other risks. The third factor is your tenure in this organization of 1-5 years, which also leans toward leaving. Beyond these, your low job satisfaction, lack of recognition, and feeling you did not get the deserved promotion further increase the likelihood of leaving. To address this, the organization should discuss your career path and satisfaction, consider recognition and development opportunities, and explore whether your extensive experience could be better utilized to keep you engaged. You may also reflect on what would make you stay.
